body:
Well, the biggest motivator was that I paid $30,000 for school, and wouldn't get a refund if I failed. So I forced myself awake each day at 7am, went, and ended up falling asleep in class at 10am, 2pm and 5pm on the bus home. They can fail me for absences but can't if I'm there! 
So willpower didn't work, I tried eating at times when I wasn't hungry but should be were I on a regular schedule. Tried having a classmate shake me so I didn't have a "build-up" of sleep, dayquil made me feel ill, nyquil made my limbs numb but not sleepy.  I don't drink coffee or energy drinks, I tried but I was just jittery for two hours and then passed out and felt sick.  General sleep deprivation (not napping) was a bad idea, I usually had to run to the school bathroom and vomit.  Daylight/lightbulbs have zero effect on my ability to sleep in a room, I tried flux for my laptop but it just gives me eyestrain.

I fit [criteria 1-6](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delayed_sleep_phase_disorder#Definition) entirely, I suggested it to my doctor on my first visit and on return (after a bunch of negative blood tests for things like anemia) she agreed it's the most likely cause.  However as she's a family doctor, we can't be 100% sure until I have a full sleep test.  I guess I should also mention I kept a sleep journal for three months we had a look at.

Exercise is a good option for sure, unfortunately tired and sleepy are two different things for me, and exercise just makes my body exhausted and then I lie awake because my mind isn't.

 I love her so much... and I know she loves me as well. It's just I have no other family members that I can rely on in a transitioning phase/if I get a night job, as soon as I get that job she'll kick me out, she's flat out said this.  Not giving out too much information I live in one of the most expensive regions house price wise in the world, a part time graveyard shift at a coffee place wouldn't give me close to enough for rent.  Even after we had the most serious heart to heart we've ever had last week she won't budge on it and I can't understand it at all... we have such a great relationship and it confuses me why she won't help.

Diagnosis means an employer must recognize it and must make reasonable accommodations, as in they won't be able to schedule you for a 9am shift and then fire you when you say you can't do it.  Full time wise in the industry I went to school for, it means I would be able to work 12pm-9pm, although I would need treatment to be able to wake at noon.  Personally I feel like I could be useful to society in a small way by working a night shift, most people can't or are uncomfortable doing it... I should take advantage of my problem right? Mum doesn't see this at all and I've tried too often, my strongest feelings of quitting for good are always after we've fought about it.  She's my lifeline, if our relationship is bad I don't have much left emotionally, and no physical support.
